ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons per Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations; mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, shareholders, and signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Terrorist List, and the Egyptian Terrorist Entities and Persons List maintained by the Ministry of Justice; commercial digital media platforms must verify ultimate beneficial owners at the 25% ownership threshold or control standard and update records within 30 days of any change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Online Company Name Reservation System via the Investor Services Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arabic is the official incorporation language; all legal and commercial company names must be in Arabic script. A Latin-script secondary name may be registered for international use but must be transliterated consistently in all commercial and tax filings. The name may not duplicate, confusingly resemble, or include unapproved state-linked terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and is not extendable; after expiry the same name may be re-reserved if it remains available. Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with GAFI's Names Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notice, attaching a trademark clearance search, corporate purpose explanation, and evidence of distinctiveness. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may either resubmit a new name after a 5-working-day cooling-off period or initiate annulment proceedings against the rejection before the Administrative Court of Cairo.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk stock-photo and generative visual assets entity as a registered service address, provided the virtual office lease is documented, the address is physically located in Egypt, and the office accepts service of judicial and regulatory process during normal business hours. The Egyptian tax authority and GAFI may require evidence of a staffed physical reception point, and bank account domiciliation may additionally require a residential or physical commercial lease.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated 10% likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection by GAFI or the Egyptian tax authority within the first 24 months for a fully digital card-fed stock media company. Likelihood increases to 30% if cash collection, high-volume manual invoicing, or offline commercial premises are introduced.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 Concerning Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 1-50 governing Limited Liability Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registration Department, Ministry of Trade and Industry

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement; capital determined by partners and must be fully paid in cash at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of the newly incorporated Egyptian LLC resolves as follows: The initial quota capital is subscribed by the founders in agreed proportions. The registered office is adopted at the designated address in Egypt. Officers are appointed including a Managing Director, Financial Manager, and Company Secretary. All actions necessary for statutory compliance, including filing with the Companies Department, obtaining the Commercial Registration, and opening a corporate bank account, are authorized. The Board shall meet regularly to oversee operations and ensure full compliance with Egyptian commercial law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA / Maslaha al-Dara'ib al-Misriyya), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt; principal portals: https://www.eta.gov.eg (tax registration, Tax Card, returns) and https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg (e-invoice/e-receipt real-time clearance).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the LLC via GAFI or the Commercial Registry and obtain the Commercial Registration certificate. Step 2: Within 30 days of incorporation, file with the ETA the Tax Card application (articles of association, CR, authenticated shareholder passports, registered office lease) to obtain the permanent Tax Card number (the primary TIN). Step 3: File VAT registration concurrently if projected annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000; a non-resident parent or digital platform shareholder must separately register under the ETA simplified non-resident digital-services VAT module (no Egyptian notarization; filing by home-country TIN, passport copy, and an Egyptian tax representative or designated online channel). Step 4: Complete ETA e-invoicing onboarding and obtain the two digital signature certificates (signature key and encryption key) for fiscal clearance. Step 5: Open a CBE-licensed bank account and establish the exporter's foreign-currency proceeds register for FX receipt tracking.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed on worldwide income at the standard CIT rate of 22.5% (Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005); non-resident shareholders are subject to Egyptian-source taxation only (dividend WHT 10%, royalty WHT 20% as applicable). No pass-through or transparent treatment exists for LLCs. Qualifying exporters of digital services may additionally apply the partial CIT reduction on export profits under Article 29(1) of Law 91/2005, subject to ministerial conditions and the Export Development Fund rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable to LLC classification: Egypt does not operate check-the-box or comparable flow-through elections; LLCs are mandatorily taxed at the entity level. Available statutory elections are limited to: (i) selection of fiscal year (calendar year or other ETA-approved 12-month period); (ii) VAT grouping of related resident companies with ETA prior approval; (iii) simplified non-resident digital VAT registration; and (iv) sector-specific export procedure reconfirmation. There is no domestic hybrid mismatch election; treaty benefit and LOB analysis is applied contractually rather than by elective filing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended by Law No. 24 of 2017 and subsequent decrees; invoice-based, non-cumulative, administered by the VAT and E-Invoicing units of the Egyptian Tax Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies for resident taxable persons (Article 22, VAT Law 67/2016); there is NO de minimis threshold for non-resident suppliers of electronically supplied services (digital content, stock media, SaaS, AI-generated visual assets) — registration is triggered upon the first supply to an Egyptian consumer under the ETA simplified non-resident digital VAT module.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance: B2B invoices must be issued in valid JSON/XML and transmitted to the ETA e-invoicing platform (https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg) for validation; the ETA returns a Unique Identifier and a cryptographic QR stamp before the invoice is legally effective. B2C transactions are covered by the parallel e-receipt system requiring fiscal integration of ERPs/cash registers with the ETA API. Enrollment is phased by cumulative turnover brackets; connections use OAuth2-secured APIs with digital certificates and the ETA e-invoicing JSON schema. Invoices failing clearance are treated as non-issued and input VAT deduction is denied; penalties up to EGP 50,000 per invoice may apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 16 of VAT Law 67/2016: zero-rating applies to services genuinely exported from Egypt — supplied to a non-resident customer, consumed outside Egypt, consideration received in freely convertible foreign currency, and statutory export evidence retained. For the stock-photography/generative visual assets LLC: sales of licenses, subscriptions, API deliveries, and AI-generated visual content to non-resident end-users qualify for 0% VAT where the contract is with a non-resident, payment is received in FX into an Egyptian bank account, and download/use occurs outside Egypt. Supplies to Egyptian residents or where the digital asset is enjoyed in Egypt are standard-rated at 14%; intra-Egypt distribution is not zero-rate eligible.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA-cleared zero-rated export e-invoice (valid QR code, export/digital services code)

For physical media only: Customs Export Declaration plus Bill of Lading or Airway Bill; for pure digital export: non-customs digital-supply evidence (server logs, licensee geolocation, download attestation, AI-platform usage record)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) / CBE bank foreign-exchange receipt evidencing receipt of the export consideration in convertible currency
Executed license agreement, purchase order, or API subscription record with the non-resident customer and IP address/geolocation data of the delivery endpoint
CBE export proceeds register entry confirming FX repatriation within the statutory 180-day window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may re-audit zero-rated exports for 5 years (10 years for suspected fraud). Failure to produce the full documentation bundle within 90 days of an ETA request retroactively revokes zero-rating, triggering assessment at 14% VAT plus monthly late-payment interest of 2% (or the CBE discount rate, if higher) and forfeiture of the refund claim. Proven evasion attracts an additional penalty of 100%–200% of the tax due (Articles 42–43, VAT Law) and imprisonment under Articles 72–75. Non-repatriation of export FX within the CBE 180-day deadline denies the export proof, imposes a 10% administrative penalty on the un-repatriated amount under CBE Foreign-Exchange Regulations, and disqualifies the exporter from the refund fast-track and Export Development Fund support.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed floating exchange rate regime administered by the Central Bank of Egypt. Current account transactions are convertible with standard documentation requirements. Capital account transactions, including equity contributions and profit remittances, require prior Central Bank of Egypt approval and are subject to repatriation ceilings, tax withholding, and documentation verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds must be surrendered to an authorized Egyptian bank within six months from the date of shipment. The surrendering bank must receive full commercial documentation including invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin. Non-surrender constitutes a regulatory violation subject to penalties and account restrictions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for offshore electronic money institutions. CBE regulations prohibit unlicensed cross-border digital payment services and impose strict AML/KYC obligations on any foreign EMI operating within Egypt.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and authorized signatories is mandatory for KYC interviews and account opening. Remote digital onboarding is not permitted for cross-border corporate entities under current CBE rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership disclosure or source of funds verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of beneficial ownership, bank statements, tax returns, and legal entity documents
Detailed transaction history, third-party verification reports, and CBE compliance affidavits

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION'. Include board resolution, share subscription agreement, and proof of ownership. Banks require CBE pre-approval for equity inflows exceeding regulatory thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes reflecting the transaction (e.g., 'GOODS SUPPLY') or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit confirmed by Egyptian banks. All payments require supporting trade documents and may trigger FX surrender obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll and Salary Withholding Tax Recap Statement (employer annual payroll tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Tax Card electronic file / salary tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 28 February for the preceding calendar year; underlying monthly salary WHT remitted by the 15th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% per month delay penalty on unpaid WHT; administrative fine up to EGP 20,000 for employer non-filing; enforced collection after 30-day notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Establishment Statement (Form 1) and monthly insured-persons declarations (Form 2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual establishment statement by 31 January of the following year; monthly contribution declarations by the 15th of each following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 1.5% per month on arrears; misdeclaration fines of EGP 1,000 - 10,000; repeated default can trigger administrative attachment and manager travel restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 45) with audited financial statements, WHT recaps, and transfer-pricing disclosure where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - competent tax district / unified national e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; 30 April for a 31 December year-end; advance corporate tax prepayments applied quarterly under the instalment regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% per month late-payment penalty on unpaid tax; fixed administrative penalty of EGP 10,000 or more for non-filing; enforced assessment, asset attachment, and blocking of the electronic tax certificate if not resolved within the cure notice period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax returns and e-invoice compliance (12 monthly filing cycles per year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - VAT e-filing and e-invoicing platforms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, by the 15th day of the calendar month following each VAT period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% per month delay penalty on VAT due; e-invoice issuance failures attract fines of EGP 20,000 - 100,000 per non-compliant transaction; failure to register or file can also trigger suspension of tax clearance certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly of Shareholders - approval of audited financial statements and filing of the signed resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) / competent Commercial Registry office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly to be convened within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); resolution and audited FS filed within 30 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Companies Law 159/1981 fines of EGP 5,000 - 50,000 for failure to hold the annual meeting or to appoint an auditor; GAFI cure notices followed by Commercial Registry strike-off action after persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial (Governorate) License annual renewal and Egyptian Chamber of Commerce annual subscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Governorate Trade and Industry Licensing Directorate (e.g., Cairo) and the General Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually aligned to the Governorate renewal cycle, generally in Q4-Q1; renewal must be completed before the license expiry date stated on the current certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of 10% - 25% of the license fee; operating with an expired license may result in closure orders, fines of EGP 5,000 - 20,000, and refusal of government clearance documents

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) annual confirmation through the Commercial Registry corporate file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry office / GAFI corporate database (AML coordination)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed together with the license renewal window (Q1-Q2); any shareholding transfer or UBO change must additionally be declared within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 80/2002 fines of EGP 20,000 - 500,000 for false or missing UBO declarations; repeated non-confirmation can block Commercial Registry transactions and lead to administrative strike-off after a 60-90 day cure notice

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs must appoint at least one licensed Egyptian auditor irrespective of size under Companies Law 159/1981 (Articles 158-160); additionally, audited financial statements must accompany the corporate tax return where annual turnover exceeds EGP 5 million (approx. USD 105,000), which applies to this stock-photo and generative visual assets platform in the ordinary course
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially converged with IFRS, are mandatory for entities governed by the Companies Law and are required for corporate tax compilation under Income Tax Law 91/2005

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO and shareholding detail is recorded with the Commercial Registry; any transfer of membership interests must be reflected in the Register of Members within 21 days and reported to the Commercial Registry/GAFI within 30 days; an annual confirmation of the same data is filed during the license-renewal cycle, and because the platform processes online payment flows through Stripe/PayPal, the company must also apply customer due diligence and internal AML filing protocols applicable to DNFBPs under AML Law 80/2002
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: General Assembly Minute Book and Attendance Register
Journal and General Ledger (statutory accounting books)
Commercial Registry license file with supporting corporate documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 500 - 1,500 per annum for a mid-size low-risk stock-media LLC with cross-border payment flows
